Determination: Adverse determination - level of care, inpatient versus observation

NOTICE OF ADVERSE DETERMINATION

Meridian Health Plan has completed review of the inpatient admission identified above. Based on the clinical information submitted, an adverse determination has been issued regarding the level of care billed. The requested inpatient level of care is not approved. The services provided could have been delivered safely at a lower level of care, such as observation.

BASIS FOR DETERMINATION

This review applied the InterQual-style criteria set in effect on the date of service. The following criteria codes were found not met:

CHF-01: Oxygen saturation at presentation did not show hypoxemia requiring inpatient oxygen therapy.

CHF-03: There was no documented trial of intensified outpatient therapy before admission.

No other criteria codes were applied to this determination.

CLAIM ADJUSTMENT CODING

The following codes apply to the associated claim:

CARC CO-50
RARC N130

This is an adverse determination of level of care only, inpatient versus observation. The member is not financially liable beyond applicable benefit cost sharing for covered services rendered at the appropriate level of care.

APPEAL RIGHTS

The member, or a provider acting as the member's authorized representative, may request a Level 1 appeal. Appeals may be submitted by letter or by portal upload. The appeal submission should cite the criteria codes inline, specifically CHF-01 and CHF-03, and address the findings stated above. Please attach the History and Physical and the progress notes covering the admission. Appeal submissions are subject to a five page limit, excluding attached medical records. Appeals must be received by [[APPEAL_DEADLINE]].

A copy of the specific criteria used in this review is available upon request at no charge. A physician reviewer is available to discuss this determination with the attending provider upon request through the Utilization Management Department.

This determination was made by a physician reviewer.

Sincerely,

Medical Director, Utilization Management
